sections.h2: Which routes get a New Brunswick house sold fast?
sections.html:
Three paths are open to a New Brunswick owner. An agent listing reaches the most buyers, a private sale saves the fee, and a direct as-is purchase trades some price for speed. Whichever you pick, the deed is recorded at the Middlesex County Clerk's office on Bayard Street, inside the city.

This is a renter city. Census QuickFacts shows an owner-occupied rate of just 21.4% for 2020 to 2024, spread over 15,676 households of about 3.13 people each. A sale here often involves a house with tenants or a landlord seller, so the rental rules covered below matter as much as the repair list.

  • Agent listing: the widest exposure, though showings, repairs and a lender's timetable come with it.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you still need an attorney, a deed and the municipal paperwork.
  • As-is purchase: often no lender and a closing date you set, with the house taken in its current state.

sections.h2: What is New Brunswick like as a place to sell?
sections.html:
New Brunswick holds 5.23 square miles of land along the Raritan River in Middlesex County. Across the water sit Piscataway, Highland Park and Edison, while North Brunswick, East Brunswick and Somerset County's Franklin Township share its other borders. QuickFacts lists a July 2025 estimate of 57,133 people.

The first European settlement dates to 1681, and the name New Brunswick arrived in 1714. A town charter in 1736 became a city charter in 1784. Rutgers began as Queen's College in 1766 and settled here in 1771, and Old Queens, finished in 1811, remains the oldest building on campus.

Residents refer to the Fifth Ward, Feaster Park, Lincoln Park, Raritan Gardens and Edgebrook-Westons Mills. When you describe your house to a buyer, naming the section it sits in gives a clearer picture than the street address alone. Winters bring about 29 inches of snow a season with roughly 50 inches of total precipitation a year, so clear gutters and check the roof before the first showing.

sections.h2: Who looks for homes in New Brunswick?
sections.html:
Hospital staff, students and commuters make up much of the demand. City Hall promotes the Health Care City nickname, and Johnson & Johnson keeps its global headquarters here beside several medical teaching and research institutions. Rutgers has three campuses inside city limits, and Robert Wood Johnson Medical School spans New Brunswick and Piscataway.

Commuting also shapes who looks at a house. Residents spend 23.3 minutes getting to work on average, and the city sits on the Northeast Corridor rail line between New York and Trenton. Route 18, U.S. 1 and Route 27 cross the city, and a short piece of the New Jersey Turnpike touches it.

Schools matter to families. The New Brunswick Public Schools run 12 schools with about 9,690 students, are one of the former Abbott districts, and include a health sciences high school tied to a teaching hospital. The Greater Brunswick Charter School serves grades K to 8, and eighth graders countywide can apply to the Middlesex County magnet schools.

  • Hospital and university staff looking for a short commute.
  • Landlords weighing a rental house against the city's rent control rules.
  • Households who want rail access to Penn Station.

sections.h2: What local steps come before a New Brunswick closing?
sections.html:
Begin with the alarm check. New Brunswick's Division of Fire Safety inspects smoke detectors and carbon monoxide alarms in one and two family houses being sold or leased, and it offers an online form for booking the visit. Schedule it early so a dead battery does not push the closing back.

The Construction Department, at 25 Kirkpatrick Street, also issues a Certificate of Continuing Occupancy for situations where the city calls for one. Phone 732-745-5075 and ask whether your sale needs it, since the answer depends on the property and its permit history.

If tenants live in the house, read the Rent Control Ordinance before you list. Most rental units in the city are regulated, and each regulated unit must register by April 1 every year. Owners of unregistered units face summonses and fines, so confirm your registration status with the Rent Control office first.

sections.h2: How does rent control affect the price of a New Brunswick rental?
sections.html:
It sets a ceiling on income. Rents may rise only by the yearly allowance unless the unit has an approved vacancy decontrol or is exempt, so the rent roll you show is the figure a buyer will underwrite.

For 2027 the city lists a $55 per unit registration fee, doubled if the form comes in after April 30. A vacancy adjustment costs $60 a unit and a market vacancy decontrol $175. The office answers questions at 732-745-5050 or rentcontrol@cityofnewbrunswick.org, and its page also describes the changes that began January 1, 2026.

sections.h2: What does the state take from a New Brunswick seller?
sections.html:
The seller pays the state's realty transfer fee when the deed is filed. It climbs in bands as the price rises, and above $350,000 a second schedule begins that reaches $4.80 for each $500 of price in the $200,000 to $550,000 band.

QuickFacts puts the middle owner-occupied value in the city at $353,800, just over that $350,000 line, so many local sales fall into the higher schedule. The settlement statement from your closing attorney will show the exact fee.

An owner who lives out of state faces one more step. At closing the seller prepays at least two percent of the deed price toward New Jersey income tax, unless an assurance on form GIT/REP-3 applies. A New Jersey resident signs the GIT/REP-3 instead, and the closing agent usually prepares whichever form fits.

sections.h2: Who records a New Brunswick deed, and what must it show?
sections.html:
Filings go to the Middlesex County Clerk's registry on the fourth floor of the County Administration Building, 75 Bayard Street. The office is open weekdays from 8:30 until 4:10, though the last arrivals are taken at 4 pm. The main line is 732-745-3002, and walk-ins are welcome, with appointments served first.

  • Everything must be legible English, properly acknowledged, with original signatures and printed names.
  • A deed carries the drafter's name after the words Prepared by, plus tax block, lot and the price.
  • A return address is required.
  • Paper filings need a cover sheet or the county adds a $20 indexing charge.

Attorneys and title companies can also submit electronically at any hour through the county's e-recording portal. Owners worried about fraud on an empty house can sign up for the clerk's email alerts, which announce any document recorded against their block and lot.

faqs.q: Can a New Brunswick house be sold while tenants are still in it?
faqs.a: Yes. A sale does not end a tenancy. Keep your rent control registration current and have each lease and the rent history on hand, because regulated units register by April 1 every year and unregistered ones risk fines.

faqs.q: Is an inspection required before selling a small home in New Brunswick?
faqs.a: At minimum a smoke and carbon monoxide alarm check through the Division of Fire Safety for one and two family houses. Call the Construction Department at 732-745-5075 to learn whether a Certificate of Continuing Occupancy is also needed.

faqs.q: Which office files the deed after a New Brunswick sale?
faqs.a: The Middlesex County Clerk's registry, in the County Administration Building on Bayard Street. Your closing attorney or title company usually submits it, either on paper or electronically.

faqs.q: I own the house but live in another state. What changes?
faqs.a: You complete a GIT/REP form at the closing table. A nonresident seller prepays at least two percent of the deed price toward state income tax unless the GIT/REP-3 assurances apply, and can request a refund later if less is owed.

faqs.q: What would the transfer fee be on a $350,000 New Brunswick sale?
faqs.a: The lower schedule applies at exactly $350,000: $2.00 per $500 on the first $150,000, $3.35 per $500 up to $200,000, then $3.90 per $500 on the rest. One dollar over that figure moves the whole sale to the higher schedule.
